description: We're a student-led team passionate about physics, mathematics, computer science and space exploration. Our goal is to combine scientific reasoning with innovative software development to tackle real challenges using NASA's research and data. We're particularly interested in computational modelling, data analysis and interactive applications. We welcome collaborators with skills in programming, scientific research, AI, web development and data visualisation.
summary:
FIREBREAK is a web-based platform we developed to make NASA's research into combustion in microgravity easier to explore and understand. NASA has carried out numerous experiments investigating how flames behave in space, but the findings are spread across different studies and datasets, making it difficult to compare results and identify useful patterns.

Our project aims to bring this research together in one place, making it easier to examine experimental findings, understand the factors affecting combustion and explore their implications for spacecraft fire safety.

As space missions become longer and plans for permanent lunar habitats develop, understanding how fire behaves outside Earth's gravity is increasingly important. We wanted to make this research more accessible while highlighting the scientific questions that still need investigating.
details:
Before developing FIREBREAK, we looked into NASA's microgravity combustion research, particularly the BASS-II investigation. We were interested in how factors such as oxygen concentration, airflow and fuel type affect combustion, and why these findings matter for future space missions.

One issue we identified was how scattered the research is across different experiments and datasets. We wanted to bring this information together in a way that made it easier to explore, compare and understand.

FIREBREAK is our attempt to address this through an interactive web platform. We focused on presenting the research clearly, highlighting important experimental findings and exploring their implications for spacecraft fire safety.

We used AI-assisted development tools to help implement the platform, alongside our own project planning and investigation of the scientific material.
